examples.ko: 아침에 보니 창문이 깨끗하게 닦여 있어요.
examples.en: This morning I saw that the windows had been wiped clean.

examples.ko: 이 얼룩은 아무리 문질러도 안 닦여요.
examples.en: This stain won't come off no matter how much I rub it.
After mopping, the floor was wiped clean and shiny.

examples.ko: 이 천은 먼지가 잘 닦이는 것 같아요.
examples.en: This cloth seems to wipe dust off well.

examples.ko: 아직 닦이지 않은 접시가 하나 남았어요.
examples.en: There is one plate left that hasn't been wiped yet.

examples.ko: 말끔히 닦인 신발을 보니 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: I feel good seeing the shoes wiped spotless.

explain: '닦다'의 피동이라서 닦는 사람보다 닦이는 물건과 그 상태를 말할 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '닦아지다'도 써요. 사람이 닦았다고 말할 때는 '닦아 놨어요'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: This is the passive of '닦다' and focuses on the thing being wiped and its state rather than the person. '닦아지다' is used with a similar meaning. When saying a person wiped something, '닦아 놨어요' sounds more natural.

examples.en: Please write your name on the top of the box.
The top of the desk has turned white with dust.
The top of the cake is covered in cream.

examples.ko: 윗면을 위로 해서 놓아야 깨지지 않아요.
examples.en: Put it with the top side facing up so it doesn't break.
The color of the top side is different from the bottom.
The wrapping paper on top has torn.

explain: 반대말은 '아랫면'이에요. 상자, 책상, 케이크처럼 모양이 있는 물건의 위쪽 면을 말할 때 써요. 방향만 말할 때는 그냥 '위쪽'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '아랫면' (bottom side). It is used for the top surface of an object with a shape, such as a box, desk or cake. If you only mean direction, you simply say '위쪽'.

examples.en: The windowpane is broken, so wind comes in.
A ball flew over and nearly broke the windowpane.
In winter, steam fogs up the windowpane.
I brought a rag to clean the windowpanes.
This house is quiet because the windowpanes are thick.
I can hear raindrops hitting the windowpane.

explain: 창문에 끼워진 유리 그 자체를 가리켜요. 창문 전체를 말할 때는 '유리창'이라고도 하는데, 깨지거나 닦거나 두께를 말할 때는 '창유리'가 잘 맞아요. '창유리가 깨지다', '창유리를 닦다'처럼 함께 써요.
explain_en: It points to the glass itself that is set in a window. For the whole window you can also say '유리창', but '창유리' fits when talking about breaking, cleaning or thickness. It goes with phrases like '창유리가 깨지다' and '창유리를 닦다'.

examples.en: It rained a lot, so the sewer got blocked.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 하수도 공사를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our neighborhood is having sewer work done.
A smell was coming up from the sewer, so I reported it.

examples.ko: 시청에서 낡은 하수도를 새로 바꾸기로 했어요.
examples.en: The city hall decided to replace the old sewer.
Water that flows into the sewer goes to a treatment plant.

examples.ko: 하수도는 우리 눈에 잘 안 보이지만 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: Sewers are hard to see, but they are absolutely necessary.

explain: 쓰고 난 더러운 물이 흘러가는 길이에요. 깨끗한 물이 들어오는 '상수도'와 짝으로 외우면 쉬워요.
explain_en: It is the system that carries away used, dirty water. It is easy to remember as a pair with '상수도', which brings in clean water.

examples.en: I arrived home, opened the front door, and went in.

examples.ko: 현관문 앞에 택배 상자가 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: A delivery box is sitting in front of the front door.
I always lock the front door when I go out.
The front door slammed shut in the wind.
For security, I changed the front door password.
I hear someone knocking on the front door.

explain: 한국 집은 현관에서 신발을 벗고 들어가요. 그래서 문 안쪽의 신발 벗는 공간을 '현관'이라고 따로 불러요. 요즘은 열쇠 대신 '도어락' 번호로 여는 집이 많아요.
explain_en: In a Korean home you take off your shoes at the entrance. That is why the shoe-removing space just inside the door has its own name, '현관'. These days many homes open with a '도어락' (digital door lock) code instead of a key.

examples.en: A long hose is lying in the garden.

examples.ko: 호스는 쓰고 나서 잘 감아 두세요.
examples.en: Please coil the hose neatly after using it.
Dad holds a hose and washes the car.
There is a hole in the hose, so water leaks.
I watered the flowerpots with a hose.
I pressed the end of the hose with my hand.

explain: '소방 호스', '고무 호스'처럼 앞에 종류를 붙여 써요. 딱딱한 금속이나 플라스틱 관은 '파이프'라고 해서 부드러운 '호스'와 구분해요.
explain_en: A type goes in front, as in '소방 호스' and '고무 호스'. Rigid metal or plastic tubes are called '파이프', which separates them from a flexible '호스'.
